walkthroughs.body_html: Each hemisphere has four lobes: frontal (thinking, planning), parietal (touch, spatial sense), temporal (hearing, memory) and occipital (vision). Damage to each lobe produces predictable deficits.

The motor cortex runs across the back of the frontal lobe and controls voluntary movement. The somatosensory cortex sits just behind it in the parietal lobe and receives touch and pain information from the body.

Broca's area (left frontal) produces speech — damage causes slow, halting speech. Wernicke's area (left temporal) understands speech — damage causes fluent but meaningless speech. These areas show localisation of function.
